diagnostic_evidence.quote: When the contact form is global, this defines a Jacobi structure on $M$.
We have chosen to stay in the restricted setting in which the line bundle is the trivial one

issues.failure_explanation: The paper restricts Jacobi structures to the trivial line bundle. For a contact structure with only a local contact form, the construction of Lambda and E depends on the choice of local form and does not give a global Jacobi structure in this sense. The same sentence goes on to say that line-bundle Jacobi structures are needed, so it contradicts itself. The claim as written is false.

failure_location.quote: In the general case, it defines a Jacobi structure;

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sentence by 'In the general case it does not define a Jacobi structure on M in the sense used here; one needs Jacobi structures on non-trivial line bundles.'
issues.overall_effect: The scope of the contact-to-Jacobi embedding is misstated. The paper's main results are used only locally, so they are not otherwise affected.
issues.title: Contact example asserts a Jacobi structure in the general (non-global form) case, contradicting its own next clause
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence correction restores a true statement and affects no later argument.

issues.failure_explanation: With h_z(x,t)=(x,zt) we have (h_z)_*(d/dt)=z d/dt, and the coefficient 1/t at the image point becomes z/s. Hence (h_z)_*Pi = z Pi, not Pi/z. In the paper's own convention (h_z)_*X = z^k X this is degree +1. It is also the degree forced by h_z^*omega = z omega for omega = Pi^{-1}. So 'Pi is -1-homogeneous with (h_z)_*Pi = Pi/z' contradicts both the explicit computation and the paper's other conventions. The 'direct computation' asserted in the proof is false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix the convention: define homogeneous Poisson by h_z^*Pi = z^{-1}Pi, equivalently (h_z)_*Pi = z Pi, and redo the one-line check.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of homogeneous Poisson manifold and the claim that the Poissonization satisfies it have the wrong degree or sign convention. With the stated degree, X_H = Pi(dH) for 1-homogeneous H would not be 0-homogeneous, as is later used.
issues.title: Poissonization claimed (-1)-homogeneous with (h_z)_*Pi = Pi/z, but the computation gives z*Pi
issues.why_classification: It is a local sign/convention correction; all constructions already use the correct effective degree.

issues.failure_explanation: The Darboux-Weinstein theorem (and its proof, which needs the primitive beta to vanish on N) requires omega_0 = omega_1 as forms on the full tangent spaces T_pM for p in N. For the zero section N, the flow of the spray fixes N pointwise with differential (dy, dxi) -> (dy + s pi dxi, dxi). Hence Omega evaluated on two vertical vectors at a zero-section point equals the integral over s of 2s pi(dxi1, dxi2), which is nonzero wherever pi is nonzero. So Omega and omega_can differ on T_pM at N, the hypothesis fails, and the existence of Psi is not justified. Only the Lagrangian condition holds: the zero section is Lagrangian for both forms. The Weinstein Lagrangian neighbourhood theorem, or a linear correction followed by Darboux-Weinstein, would be needed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the (homogeneous) Weinstein Lagrangian neighbourhood theorem to the zero section, which is Lagrangian for both Omega and omega_can, to get a homogeneous symplectomorphism Psi fixing the zero section. Then check that alpha = tau o Psi and beta = tau o phi^1_X o Psi remain a bi-realization.
issues.overall_effect: The passage from the Weinstein realization to the Karasev-type realization, with canonical symplectic form and homogeneous source and target, is unsupported. The homogeneous bi-realization used in Sections 5-6 rests on this step.
issues.title: Homogeneous Darboux-Weinstein applied to Omega and omega_can without equality on T_pM along the zero section
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a contained new argument (a different theorem and a check of the realization properties) but not a new global architecture, and the conclusion survives.

issues.failure_explanation: Poissonization of the contact example has Pi containing -(d/dt)^(d/dz), so pi^{zt} = +1. The formula alpha^i = y^i + (1/2) pi^{vi} xi_v then gives alpha^t = t + (1/2) xi_z. The other components of the displayed alpha (q, p, z) follow this rule correctly, and beta^t should be t - (1/2) xi_z. The displayed formulas have the t-components of alpha and beta swapped. Equivalently, the spray has d/dt-component -xi_z, so beta (half-forward) should have t - xi_z/2. As stated, alpha and beta are not the order-2 truncation of the Karasev realization, and the Poisson/anti-Poisson properties fail at the t-slot.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the signs in the t-components: alpha^t = t + xi_z/2 and beta^t = t - xi_z/2. Homogeneity is unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The only explicit bi-realization in the paper, the contact example, is incorrect in one component. The affected equations are eq: bi-realization example and eq: bi-realization example2.
issues.title: t-component of explicit alpha and beta has the wrong sign relative to the stated formula and the spray
issues.why_classification: It is a local sign correction in two displayed formulas, and the homogeneity check remains valid.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the induced map $\varphi_L = \beta\circ \alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ defines a Poisson diffeomorphism $(P,\Pi)\rightarrow (P,\Pi)$
the induced family of diffeomorphisms $(\varphi_{L_s})_{s\in I}$ is a homogeneous Hamiltonian Poisson integrator of order $k$ for $H^P$

issues.failure_explanation: The cited theorem says that an arbitrary Lagrangian bisection gives a Poisson diffeomorphism (item 1). Only the special bisections L_s = phi^s_{alpha^*H}(sigma(P)) give the Hamiltonian flow (item 3). A general Lagrangian bisection gives a Poisson map that need not be a Hamiltonian flow, so the stated guarantee is false. The paper then asserts that a 'suitable approximation of the variation functions' yields a homogeneous integrator of order k. Variation functions live on the bisections L_s, not on P. No argument is given that the family phi_{L_s} is the flow of a time-dependent homogeneous Hamiltonian H_s with H_s = H^P + o(s^{k-1}), that it is homogeneous, or that such an approximation exists. This is the central step of the paper and has no formal statement or proof.

failure_location.quote: Theorem \ref{thm: ham flow} guarantees that, given a Lagrangian bisection $L$, the induced diffeomorphism $\varphi_L$ is a Hamiltonian flow.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the correct form of the cited theorem (Poisson diffeo for any bisection; Hamiltonian flow for the special family). Then add a theorem with proof, adapting the PHI construction, that an exact family of homogeneous Lagrangian bisections whose variation functions pull back to H^P + o(s^{k-1}) yields an order-k hPHI. This must include the homogeneity checks.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised construction of Jacobi Hamiltonian integrators of order k is not established. Only the exact-flow case and the Poisson-diffeomorphism property are supported.
issues.title: Theorem ham flow is misstated, and the order-k hPHI construction is asserted without proof
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is a contained adaptation of known PHI results to the homogeneous setting, so the claimed result is expected to survive.

issues.failure_explanation: A JHI is required both to be a (strict) Jacobi diffeomorphism, preserving the Jacobi bracket, and to be the time-epsilon flow of a Hamiltonian H_s. For E not equal to 0, Hamiltonian flows are in general not strict Jacobi automorphisms. For the contact example, H=z gives X_H = p d/dp + z d/dz, which rescales E. They are only contactomorphisms or Jacobi maps up to a conformal factor. Homogeneous Poisson diffeomorphisms of P_J correspond to Jacobi maps with conformal factor, namely (x,t) -> (phi(x), a(x)t), not to strict ones. So the two integrator classes do not correspond as defined: either the JHI definition is nearly vacuous or the correspondence fails. The equivalence of categories invoked says nothing about Hamiltonians, flows or orders.

failure_location.quote: we can conclude that we have a $1$-to-$1$ correspondence between homogeneous Poisson Hamiltonian integrators and Jacobi Hamiltonian integrators.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine JHI with Jacobi diffeomorphisms in the generalized sense (conformal factor, or line-bundle morphisms) matching homogeneous Poisson diffeomorphisms. Then prove the dictionary for Hamiltonians H <-> tH, time-dependent flows and the order condition, instead of citing the equivalence of categories.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of Jacobi Hamiltonian integrator and the claim that the constructed hPHI projects to a JHI are inconsistent, so the guarantee that the output is a 'Jacobi diffeomorphism' is unsupported.
issues.title: Claimed 1-to-1 correspondence between hPHI and JHI conflicts with the strict Jacobi-diffeomorphism requirement in the JHI definition
issues.why_classification: The definitions can be repaired by adopting the generalized Jacobi morphisms, and the dictionary proof is routine but nontrivial; the construction itself survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: since to preserving the Poisson structure and the Hamiltonian (up to a certain order)

issues.failure_explanation: Along X_H = Lambda(.,dH) - H E, one has X_H(H) = -H E(H), which is nonzero in general. So for E not equal to 0 (the dissipative/contact case the paper advertises) H is not conserved even by the exact flow, and no integrator can 'preserve the Hamiltonian'. What can be preserved is the Poissonized Hamiltonian H^P = tH, and only up to the order of the method. The introduction itself restricts the PHI claim to 'up to a certain order', and nothing in the paper proves preservation of H, of the foliation, or of Casimirs for the actual JHI.

failure_location.quote: This approach preserves not only the Jacobi structure and the Hamiltonian, but also the induced foliation and Casimir functions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate: the method preserves the Jacobi structure in the generalized sense and the leaves, and conserves H^P = tH up to the order of the method. Remove the claim about conserving H.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised structure-preservation guarantees are overstated for the Jacobi setting.
issues.title: Conclusion claims the integrator preserves the Hamiltonian, which is false for dissipative Jacobi systems and exceeds what is proved
issues.why_classification: It is a rewording of the scope statement; the construction and its supported properties are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We want to prove that $\pi_*(h_z^*(\alpha)) = h_z^*(\pi_*(\alpha)).$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows that fibre integration pi_* commutes with h_z^*. It never introduces the contraction homotopy or the homotopy formula, never shows that a closed form equals d(pi_* alpha), and never derives homogeneity of the primitive from the commutation. The hypothesis 'homogeneous star-shaped open subset of R^n' is also inconsistent with a free R^x-action (the set is invariant under t -> -t, so it is not star-shaped about a point off the fixed locus). So the stated conclusion is not proved. A valid short argument exists (L_Z alpha = alpha for the Euler field Z, so alpha = d(i_Z alpha)), but it is not the one given.

failure_location.quote: all $1$-homogeneous closed $p$-forms are exact and their primitive is also homogeneous

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the proof by the Cartan-formula argument (closed and 1-homogeneous implies alpha = L_Z alpha = d(i_Z alpha), with i_Z alpha 1-homogeneous), and fix the hypothesis on the domain.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma, advertised as a new homogeneous Poincare lemma, is unproven as written. Its use in the Darboux-Weinstein proof is only in a vacuous case, so the other theorems are not affected.
issues.title: Proof of the homogeneous Poincare lemma never produces or checks a primitive
issues.why_classification: A short routine replacement proof preserves the lemma and all its uses.

issues.failure_explanation: The Poincare-Cartan form is defined as p dq - H dt, but the generating-function relation is written with +H dt. Using the stated form gives K = H + dF_1/dt, hence H + dS/dt = 0 for K = 0, the standard Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The displayed equation H = dS/dt, with the opposite sign, follows only from the inconsistent '+H dt' line. The sign matters for matching dS_t with the Hamiltonian flow, since the variation forms are compared to dH.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the sign consistent: use p dq - H dt - (P dQ - K dt) = dF_1, giving dS/dt + H = 0 (or flip the conventions throughout), and re-check the variation-form identification in the Hamilton-Jacobi examples.
issues.overall_effect: The Hamilton-Jacobi equation used to produce the family of Lagrangian bisections has an unjustified sign (time orientation). The identification with the Hamiltonian flow is affected, though the structure of the argument is not.
issues.title: Sign inconsistency in the derivation of the homogeneous Hamilton-Jacobi equation
issues.why_classification: It is a local sign correction in the appendix derivation and the equation; the homogeneity analysis is unaffected.
